title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-samira-gupta
body:
Quick dump of notes for PR #432 (dataset-cache refactor) - personal scratchpad.

Context:
- PR aims to replace the old dataset cache layer with a unified KV cache that supports partial key invalidation and TTL tiers.
- Motivation: reduce duplicate fetches during bursts, improve cold-start latency for batch jobs.
- Concern: compatibility with existing multi-tenant routing + on-disk fallback.

Primary review checklist (high level):
- Correctness:
  - Ensure cache key derivation is stable across restarts (include version/hash in key).
  - Confirm there's no silent data loss when switching from old format -> new format (migration path?).
  - Verify concurrency: race between write-through and eviction path.
- Safety & rollout:
  - Feature flag gating present? (yes, runtime flag: dataset_cache_v2)
  - Backwards compatibility: old nodes should still read old entries until full rollout.
  - Migration plan: gradual shadowing -> dual-write -> cutover (needs checklist).
- Performance:
  - Microbench: add mem/latency perf numbers for 1k QPS with 4k seq-length.
  - Batching interaction: ensure batching logic doesn't duplicate prefix keys.
  - Metrics: cache hit ratio, evictions/sec, `cache_write_failures` tag by reason.
- Observability:
  - Tracing: add span for cache.get/cache.put with key-hash (not raw key).
  - Logs: rate-limited warnings on serialization errors; include tenant id.
  - Dashboards: temp dashboard to track rollout signals.
- Testing:
  - Unit tests: key derivation edge cases (unicode, long prompts).
  - Integration: simulate restart + concurrent writes (use docker-compose local env).
  - Chaos: eviction + disk full scenario.

Inline code notes / questions for PR author:
- dataset_cache/serializer.py: why choose msgpack over protobuf? comment suggests speed but no bench. ask for numbers or leave as TODO.
- cache/index.py L87: locks are per-namespace but key might allow cross-namespace collisions — need clearer invariants.
- fallback logic (on-disk->s3): possible OOM if payloads large; consider streaming decompress.
- ttl tiers: config knobs exist but defaults are aggressive (5m); recommend 30m for embeddings-heavy workloads.

Refactor ideas (non-blocking):
- Extract KeyVersioning class to reduce repeated versioning code across modules.
- Introduce a thin adapter interface so Dedicated/private builds can override on-disk path.
- Move migration logic to a separate migration job binary instead of happening at runtime on first read. Easier to control and monitor.

Follow-ups & action items:
- @Avery: add microbench results and update PR description with numbers (due: 2026-02-18).
- @Evan: add integration test that simulates dual-write shadowing.
- @Ravi: review TLS/permissions on S3 fallback path (check KMS usage).
- Add canary rollout playbook to ops-runbook (small percentage -> 25% -> 100%).

Open questions to resolve before merge:
- Do we need to support read-conversion of old-format keys, or can we invalidate on first traffic? (owner preference: dual-read for safety)
- Are there regulatory implications for storing partial prompts on disk? check with security/compliance.
- Can we make the default TTL configurable per-model to avoid one-size-fits-all?

Scratch TODOs (personal):
- Draft short Slack summary for #eng-serving-runtime after merge (1-2 bullets + link).
- Add a snippet to developer handbook about cache versioning.
- If migration job chosen, write quick runbook and add to Confluence.

Random notes / brain dump:
- Watch out for tests that assume deterministic eviction order (some integration tests broke before).
- Might be worth a follow-up PR to centralize cache metric labels (tenant, model, region).
- If messagepack kept, add schema version prefix to serialized blob.

References used in review:
- previous PR that introduced on-disk fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-cache/pull/312
- infra jira for cache incidents last quarter: INF-1540

End of scratchpad. Keep this document as ephemeral — will transfer key items to PR checklist in repo once decisions made.
